reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify the refunds table matches Alpha's reported refunds, so I'll start by listing refunds.
The refunds table matches Alpha's reported refunds exactly (orders 272, 274, 275 with the same amounts), so I can proceed. Next I need the orders to identify the customers to pay.

The refunds table matches Alpha's report exactly, so I can proceed. The orders name three customers (acme, birch, cobalt), and I need each one's net balance before recording payouts, so I'll start with acme.
Acme's net balance is 62169 and the refunds table matched Alpha's report, so I can record acme's payout. Next I'll check birch and cobalt's net balances.
Acme's payout is recorded. Next I'll get birch's net balance, since the figure comes from net_balance and I shouldn't compute it myself.
Birch's net balance from net_balance is 48740, and the refunds already matched Alpha's report, so I'll record birch's payout. Cobalt is still outstanding after that.
Acme and birch are paid, and the refunds matched Alpha's report. Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll get its net balance from net_balance before recording a payout.

Cobalt's net_balance is 24373, which matches orders 272 and 275 (35333) minus refunds 272 and 275 (10960). The refunds matched Alpha's report, so I'll record cobalt's payout, the last one in the batch.
All three customers have been paid. The refunds table matched Alpha's report, and each net balance matches the orders minus the refunds for that customer. Reporting the payouts now.
